name: Harbor
subtitle: Energy · housing · workforce
question: Which investments can cut household energy burden without displacing residents?
context: A fictional regional compact covers 1,200 occupied homes and a constrained district energy network. The compact has a $60 million appropriation, a 36-month projection, two municipal partners and an independent resident assembly. Procurement quotes, consent records and workforce estimates disagree. The figures below are synthetic planning proxies, not an engineering assessment.
authority: Harbor compact board; resident assembly consent is required for work in occupied homes.
principles: Resident consent can be withdrawn before work begins.
Regional emissions must not rise above the starting estimate.
Treat contested estimates as revisable claims, not commitments.

scopes.name: Harbor compact
scopes.description: Two municipalities coordinate an appropriation of $60 million over 36 months. Neither owns the resident assembly nor the training college.

scopes.name: District network
scopes.description: Substation commissioning and heat-network work share scarce electrical crews. Utility consent does not authorize entry into homes.

scopes.name: Occupied housing
scopes.description: 1,200 homes; 480 currently meet the compact's winter comfort threshold. Tenants retain separate consent rights.

scopes.name: Skills partnership
scopes.description: The college and two unions can certify additional installers; training hours cannot substitute for qualified crew hours.

scopes.name: Resident assembly
scopes.description: An independent institution representing residents in both municipalities. Consent is bounded by the signed register, not assumed from participation.

scopes.name: Transition fund
scopes.description: The appropriation funds complete packages. Unspent authority is available for contingencies; it is not additional capacity.

objectives.label: Emissions
objectives.description: Synthetic annual regional energy emissions index. Reductions add as a planning approximation; rebound and interactions remain outside this first model.

objectives.label: Warm homes
objectives.description: Occupied homes expected to meet the winter comfort threshold. A home is counted once within each proposed package; forecasts cannot exceed the 1,200-home stock.

objectives.label: Qualified installers
objectives.description: People with the agreed safety certification; forecast completion is not an employment guarantee.

objectives.label: Involuntary moves
objectives.description: A protected limit, independent of financial or carbon benefits. Any planned involuntary move makes a portfolio inadmissible.

objectives.label: Energy burden
objectives.description: Median modeled household energy expenditure as a share of disposable income. Tariff and technical savings are uncertain, additive proxies.

source.title: Appropriation ledger · synthetic
source.author: Evan Moss
source.excerpt: The compact has $60 million of spending authority for the 36-month period. This excludes an unapproved $15 million application.

claims.label: Qualified crew hours

source.title: Contractor availability return · synthetic
source.author: Jun Park
source.excerpt: Three contractors list 18,000 qualified hours across the compact's work period. One 8,500-hour listing is also offered to a neighboring region.

claims.dissent: The neighboring procurement may reduce our confirmed allocation to 9,500 hours.

source.title: College and union allocation · synthetic
source.author: Luis Moreno
source.excerpt: The signed allocation contains 7,200 instructor and supervised-practice hours. Seats require trainees to opt in; hours do not compel attendance.

source.title: Consent register · synthetic
source.author: Cora Bell
source.excerpt: 420 households signed package-specific provisional permissions. No nonresponse is counted as consent; withdrawals must reduce this allocation before a new decision.

source.title: Utility connection letter · synthetic
source.author: Jun Park
source.excerpt: Eight MVA are reserved for the compact after commissioning. The letter does not guarantee the commissioning date.

claims.label: Commissioning lead

source.title: Commissioning window · synthetic
source.author: Jun Park
source.excerpt: The utility proposes commissioning 12 months after mandate acceptance. Transformer procurement has not yet been completed.

claims.dissent: The equipment vendor gives a 24–30 month range if the current slot is lost.

source.title: Winter pilot extrapolation · synthetic
source.author: Amara Diallo
source.excerpt: The baseline response ratio is 1.0, extrapolated from 28 treated homes. Weather, ventilation behavior and building condition may reduce that response; no region-wide effect has been observed.

claims.label: Installed-cost index

source.title: Tender reconciliation · synthetic
source.author: Evan Moss
source.excerpt: The working quote uses a 1.2 cost index against the original estimate. The heat-loop tender excludes two road crossings.

claims.dissent: The infrastructure committee expects a 1.5 index once road permissions are priced.

interventions.title: Commission the network
interventions.mechanism: Reserve transformer delivery and commission the district connection before dependent housing work begins.

interventions.title: Treat the winter cohort
interventions.mechanism: Insulate and rebalance 80 consenting homes with current qualified crews; retain a measured comparison cohort.

interventions.title: Certify the next cohort
interventions.mechanism: Fund 90 opt-in trainees through the college and union certification pathway; do not count their hours as crew capacity in this portfolio.

interventions.title: Retrofit 280 homes
interventions.mechanism: Combine insulation, ventilation and heat-pump work after network commissioning and certification. Only separately reserved crew hours supply the work.

interventions.title: Build the shared heat loop
interventions.mechanism: Connect a separate 240-home consenting cohort to district heat after commissioning. Road-crossing cost remains contested.

interventions.title: Offer a resident tariff
interventions.mechanism: Enroll a separate 120-household cohort in a voluntary tariff with a capped winter price. Enrolment and exit remain opt-in.

interventions.title: Clear and rebuild the block
interventions.mechanism: A developer proposes demolition and fast replacement. The proposal entails 22 involuntary moves and conflicts with the compact's protected resident limit.

strategies.name: Winter first
strategies.thesis: Build evidence and skills while relieving immediate bills. Preserve capital and avoid committing to the contested network window.

strategies.name: Homes and skills
strategies.thesis: Commit to a deeper 280-home transition, contingent on network commissioning. Reserve the full work package before agents begin.

strategies.name: Build everything
strategies.thesis: Test the advertised fast transformation against shared resources and resident protections. High modeled benefits cannot override either constraint.

shocks.name: Crews allocated elsewhere
shocks.description: The neighboring region accepts the overlapping contractor offer. Our confirmed qualified crew allocation falls from 18,000 to 9,500 hours.

shocks.name: Transformer slot lost
shocks.description: A vendor notice moves commissioning to month 30. Dependent housing work finishes after the 36-month projection and contributes no benefit inside it.
